headline: Intel gave new details of its D270 AI server chip, built with large memory to run bigger AI models and cooled by air.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: details were first given on 12 Oct and no price or release date exists; specs are Intel's claims.
importance_line: It could give AI service operators a lower-cost option beyond Nvidia, but only selected customers are testing it and speed is unproven.
summary: The Gadgeteer reports that Intel, at the Open Compute Project summit on 12 October, detailed its D270 server chip for running AI models, a card with 160GB of memory that partners can extend to 480GB and that needs only air cooling. Selected customers are sampling it, Intel gave no price or release date, and the model-size limits it quotes are its own claims that do not show how fast answers arrive.
notes: Same chip appears in C08-13 (MarketBeat angle).
